99	def _normalize_mix(mix: object) -> dict[str, int]:
100	    if not isinstance(mix, dict) or not mix:
101	        raise ValueError("mix must be a non-empty object")
102	    normalized: dict[str, int] = {}
103	    for source, share in mix.items():
104	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
105	            raise ValueError("mix sources must be non-empty strings")
106	        if not _is_plain_int(share) or share < 0:
107	            raise ValueError("mix shares must be non-boolean non-negative "
108	                             "integers")
109	        if source in normalized:
110	            raise ValueError("mix sources must be distinct")
111	        normalized[source] = share
112	    if sum(normalized.values()) != _MIX_TOTAL:
113	        raise ValueError("mix shares must sum to ten thousand")
114	    # Stored in code-point order like every other canonical mapping.
115	    return {source: normalized[source] for source in sorted(normalized)}

118	def _check_values(signal: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
119	    region = signal["region"]

121	        raise ValueError("region must be a non-empty string")
122

124	        value = signal[name]

126	            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a non-boolean non-negative "

159	def _validate_structure(data: object) -> tuple[
160	    dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, str],
161	    dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
162	]:
163	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_ROOT_FIELDS):
164	        raise ValueError("signal file root must be an object with keys "
165	                         "version, history, idempotency and audit")
166	
167	    version = data["version"]
168	    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _VERSION:
169	        raise ValueError("unsupported signal file version")
170	
171	    history_raw = data["history"]
172	    idempotency_raw = data["idempotency"]
173	    audit_raw = data["audit"]
174	    if not isinstance(history_raw, dict) \
175	            or not isinstance(idempotency_raw, dict) \
176	            or not isinstance(audit_raw, dict):
177	        raise ValueError("history, idempotency and audit must be objects")
178	    _check_sorted_keys(history_raw, "history")
179	    _check_sorted_keys(idempotency_raw, "idempotency")
180	    _check_sorted_keys(audit_raw, "audit")
181	
182	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
183	    for region, records_raw in history_raw.items():
184	        if not isinstance(region, str) or not region:
185	            raise ValueError("regions must be non-empty strings")
186	        if not isinstance(records_raw, list) or not records_raw:
187	            raise ValueError("history must hold a non-empty record list "
188	                             "per region")
189	        records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
190	        for index, record in enumerate(records_raw, start=1):
191	            if not isinstance(record, dict) \
192	                    or set(record.keys()) != set(_RECORD_FIELDS):
193	                raise ValueError("signal record has invalid fields")
194	            if record["region"] != region:
195	                raise ValueError("signal record region does not match its "
196	                                 "key")
197	            if not _is_plain_int(record["version"]) \
198	                    or record["version"] != index:
199	                raise ValueError("versions must be consecutive from 1")
200	            _check_values(record)
201	            if records and record["observed"] <= records[-1]["observed"]:
202	                raise ValueError("signal observations must increase across "
203	                                 "versions")
204	            records.append({
205	                "region": region,
206	                "version": index,
207	                "observed": record["observed"],
208	                "expires": record["expires"],
209	                "mix": dict(record["mix"]),
210	                "unit_cost": record["unit_cost"],
211	                "carbon_intensity": record["carbon_intensity"],
212	            })
213	        history[region] = records
214	
215	    idempotency: dict[str, str] = {}
216	    for key, region in idempotency_raw.items():
217	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
218	            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
219	        if not isinstance(region, str) or not region or region not in history:
220	            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must reference a published "
221	                             "region")
222	        idempotency[key] = region
223	
224	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
225	    for key, event in audit_raw.items():
226	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
227	            raise ValueError("audit keys must be non-empty strings")
228	        if not isinstance(event, dict) \
229	                or set(event.keys()) != set(_EVENT_FIELDS):
230	            raise ValueError("signal audit event has invalid fields")
231	        event_key = event["key"]
232	        region = event["region"]
233	        event_version = event["version"]
234	        if event_key != key or not isinstance(event_key, str) or not event_key:
235	            raise ValueError("audit event key does not match its map key")
236	        if not isinstance(region, str) or not region or region not in history:
237	            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a published region")
238	        if not _is_plain_int(event_version) or event_version < 1 \
239	                or event_version > len(history[region]):
240	            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a published version")
241	        events[key] = {"key": event_key, "region": region,
242	                       "version": event_version}
243	
244	    # The three sections describe one publication history: each
245	    # idempotency key binds one region and one publish event, the map and
246	    # the event agree on the region, and every published version is bound
247	    # to exactly one event.
248	    if set(idempotency) != set(events):
249	        raise ValueError("idempotency keys and audit events do not match")
250	    for key, region in idempotency.items():
251	        if events[key]["region"] != region:
252	            raise ValueError("audit event does not match its idempotency "
253	                             "entry")
254	    published = {(region, record["version"])
255	                 for region, records in history.items()
256	                 for record in records}
257	    bound = {(event["region"], event["version"])
258	             for event in events.values()}
259	    if bound != published:
260	        raise ValueError("every published version must be bound to an "
261	                         "audit event")
262	
263	    return history, idempotency, events

266	def _serialize(
267	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
268	    idempotency: dict[str, str],
269	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
270	) -> bytes:
271	    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII written through, each section's
272	    # primary keys in code-point order, terminated by exactly one newline.
273	    payload = {
274	        "version": _VERSION,
275	        "history": {region: history[region] for region in sorted(history)},
276	        "idempotency": {key: idempotency[key] for key in sorted(idempotency)},
277	        "audit": {key: events[key] for key in sorted(events)},
278	    }
279	    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
280	                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
281	    return text.encode("utf-8")

284	def _load_file(realpath: str) -> tuple[
285	    dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, str],
286	    dict[str, dict[str, Any]], bytes | None
287	]:
288	    try:
289	        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
290	            raw = handle.read()
291	    except FileNotFoundError:
292	        return {}, {}, {}, None
293	
294	    try:
295	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
296	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
297	        raise ValueError(
298	            f"signal file {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
299	    try:
300	        # Negative-zero and non-finite literals are format errors.
301	        data = finite_loads(text)
302	    except ValueError as exc:
303	        raise ValueError(
304	            f"signal file {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
305	    history, idempotency, events = _validate_structure(data)
306	    # Every read entry requires the on-disk bytes to be the canonical
307	    # form: fields and keys in their original order, compact JSON with
308	    # non-ASCII written through and exactly one trailing newline.
309	    if raw != _serialize(history, idempotency, events):
310	        raise ValueError(
311	            f"signal file {realpath!r} is not in canonical compact form")
312	    return history, idempotency, events, raw

315	def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
316	    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
317	    try:
318	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
319	    finally:
320	        os.close(dir_fd)

323	def _rollback_file(realpath: str, directory: str,
324	                   old_bytes: bytes | None, first: BaseException) -> None:
325	    # Restore the exact pre-call bytes while the exclusive lock is held:
326	    # stage them back over the replaced file, or remove a file that did
327	    # not exist beforehand, then sync the directory. A failed recovery
328	    # surfaces chained after the original error.
329	    try:
330	        if old_bytes is None:
331	            try:
332	                os.unlink(realpath)
333	            except FileNotFoundError:
334	                pass
335	        else:
336	            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
337	                dir=directory, prefix=".signals-restore-", suffix=".tmp")
338	            try:
339	                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
340	                    handle.write(old_bytes)
341	                    handle.flush()
342	                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
343	                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
344	            except BaseException:
345	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
346	                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
347	                raise
348	        _fsync_directory(directory)
349	    except OSError as recovery:
350	        raise recovery from first
351	
352	
353	def _commit_file(realpath: str, payload: bytes,
354	                 old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
355	    # One durable commit for the history, the idempotency map and the
356	    # audit event: same-directory temporary, fsync, atomic replace and a
357	    # directory fsync. Any failure after the replace restores the
358	    # pre-call bytes, so an unsuccessful publish leaves the original file
359	    # byte-for-byte.
360	    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
361	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
362	        dir=directory, prefix=".signals-", suffix=".tmp")
363	    try:
364	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
365	            handle.write(payload)
366	            handle.flush()
367	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
368	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
369	    except BaseException:
370	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
371	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
372	        raise
373	    try:
374	        _fsync_directory(directory)
375	    except BaseException as first:
376	        _rollback_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
377	        raise

380	def _publish_locked(
381	    realpath: str,
382	    normalized: dict[str, Any],
383	    idempotency_key: str,
384	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
385	    idempotency: dict[str, str],
386	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
387	    old_bytes: bytes | None,
388	) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], bool]:
389	    """Apply one publication against already loaded, locked state.
390	
391	    The caller holds the per-real-path in-process lock and the
392	    cross-process exclusive flock and has loaded the current file with
393	    :func:`_load_file`; the signal has already been normalized with
394	    :func:`_normalize_signal`. Performs the idempotency replay check,
395	    appends the next version (or returns the stored record without a
396	    write on replay) and durably commits a first publication. Shared by
397	    :func:`publish` and callers that must hold several files' locks at
398	    once in resolved-path order.
399	    """
400	    region = normalized["region"]
401	    existing_region = idempotency.get(idempotency_key)
402	    if existing_region is not None:
403	        event = events[idempotency_key]
404	        existing = history[existing_region][event["version"] - 1]
405	        if {field: existing[field] for field in _SIGNAL_FIELDS} \
406	                != normalized:
407	            raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with "
408	                             "a different signal")
409	        return dict(existing), False
410	
411	    versions = history.get(region)
412	    if versions is None:
413	        versions = []
414	        history[region] = versions
415	        version = 1
416	    else:
417	        if normalized["observed"] <= versions[-1]["observed"]:
418	            raise ValueError("signal observation must increase "
419	                             "across versions")
420	        version = versions[-1]["version"] + 1
421	
422	    record: dict[str, Any] = {
423	        "region": region,
424	        "version": version,
425	        "observed": normalized["observed"],
426	        "expires": normalized["expires"],
427	        "mix": dict(normalized["mix"]),
428	        "unit_cost": normalized["unit_cost"],
429	        "carbon_intensity": normalized["carbon_intensity"],
430	    }
431	    versions.append(record)
432	    idempotency[idempotency_key] = region
433	    events[idempotency_key] = {
434	        "key": idempotency_key,
435	        "region": region,
436	        "version": version,
437	    }
438	    _commit_file(realpath,
439	                 _serialize(history, idempotency, events), old_bytes)
440	    return dict(record), True
441

443	def publish(
444	    path: str,
445	    signal: dict[str, object],
446	    idempotency_key: str,
447	) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
448	    """Persistently publish one live signal version.
449	
450	    ``path`` and ``idempotency_key`` must be non-empty strings. The
451	    signal must be an object with exactly the six top-level fields
452	    region, observed, expires, mix, unit_cost and carbon_intensity: a
453	    non-empty region string, non-boolean non-negative observation and
454	    expiration moments (booleans rejected) with the expiration not
455	    earlier than the observation, non-negative unit cost and carbon
456	    intensity, and a non-empty energy ``mix`` object whose values are
457	    non-negative integers summing to exactly ten thousand. Any deviation
458	    raises ``ValueError`` before the file is touched.
459	
460	    A first publication saves the canonical record -- the signal fields
461	    plus the next consecutive ``version`` for that region, starting at
462	    1 -- together with the idempotency binding and a publish audit event
463	    carrying the key, the region and the version, all three in one
464	    durable commit, and returns ``(record, True)``. A new version for an
465	    already observed region must carry a strictly later observation
466	    moment. Replaying the same key with an identical signal returns the
467	    stored record with ``False`` without adding an event or rewriting
468	    the file; the same key with a different signal raises
469	    ``ValueError`` and preserves the original bytes.
470	
471	    A missing parent directory raises ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid
472	    existing file (encoding, JSON, negative-zero or non-finite numbers,
473	    version, structure, ordering, canonical bytes or references) raises
474	    ``ValueError``; any other locking or I/O failure raises ``OSError``.
475	    Calls serialize across threads and processes per resolved real path.
476	    """
477	    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
478	        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
479	    if not isinstance(idempotency_key, str) or not idempotency_key:
480	        raise ValueError("idempotency_key must be a non-empty string")
481	    normalized = _normalize_signal(signal)
482	
483	    store = _get_store(path)
484	    with store.lock:
485	        # Opening the companion lock in a missing directory surfaces as
486	        # FileNotFoundError before the data file is created.
487	        with _process_lock(store.realpath):
488	            history, idempotency, events, old_bytes = _load_file(
489	                store.realpath)
490	            return _publish_locked(store.realpath, normalized,
491	                                   idempotency_key, history, idempotency,
492	                                   events, old_bytes)
493	
494	
495	def get(path: str, region: str, at: int) -> dict[str, object]:
496	    """Return the region's latest signal valid at evaluation moment ``at``.
497	
498	    ``path`` and ``region`` must be non-empty strings and ``at`` a
499	    non-boolean non-negative integer evaluation moment, else
500	    ``ValueError``. The latest record whose observation is not later
501	    than ``at`` and whose expiration is not earlier than ``at`` is
502	    returned -- when several windows cover the moment, the highest
503	    version wins. A missing signal file raises ``FileNotFoundError``; an
504	    invalid file -- including non-canonical bytes -- raises
505	    ``ValueError``; an unknown region raises ``KeyError(region)`` and
506	    the absence of any valid version ``LookupError``; any other locking
507	    or I/O failure raises ``OSError``. The call never writes, and the
508	    returned record is a fresh copy with region, version, observed,
509	    expires, mix, unit_cost and carbon_intensity.
510	    """
511	    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
512	        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
513	    if not isinstance(region, str) or not region:
514	        raise ValueError("region must be a non-empty string")
515	    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
516	        raise ValueError("at must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")
517	
518	    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
519	    with _process_lock(realpath, shared=True):
520	        history, _idempotency, _events, raw = _load_file(realpath)
521	    if raw is None:
522	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"signal file {realpath!r} does not exist")
523	    versions = history.get(region)
524	    if versions is None:
525	        raise KeyError(region)
526	
527	    valid: dict[str, Any] | None = None
528	    for record in versions:
529	        if record["observed"] <= at <= record["expires"]:
530	            valid = record
531	    if valid is None:
532	        raise LookupError(region)
533	    result = dict(valid)
534	    result["mix"] = dict(valid["mix"])
535	    return result

"""Persistent, thread-safe and multi-process live signal ledger.

The baseline registry only knows the static unit cost and carbon
intensity baked into a published resource version. This module adds an
independent ledger of live signals -- per-region observations of the
energy mix, unit cost and carbon intensity at a moment in time:

* ``history`` maps each region to its published signals, versions
  consecutive from 1 with observation moments strictly increasing
  across versions and each signal not expiring before it was observed;
* ``idempotency`` binds each publish key to the region it carried;
* ``audit`` holds one publish event per first publication, binding the
  idempotency key, the region and the version it created.

A signal carries exactly the region, the observation and expiration
moments, the energy mix (a non-empty map of source shares, integer
basis points summing to ten thousand), the unit cost and the carbon
intensity; every numeric value is a non-boolean non-negative integer.

As for the supply file, every read requires the on-disk document to be
exactly the canonical compact form :func:`_serialize` produces --
fields and keys in their fixed/code-point order, no whitespace beyond
structural tokens, non-ASCII written through and one trailing newline.

:func:`publish` appends a new signal version under an idempotency key,
and :func:`get` returns the region's latest version observed no later
than the evaluation moment and not expired at it. The signal file is
never rewritten by the read path.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import fcntl
import json
import os
import tempfile
import threading
from typing import Any, Iterator

from ._jsonio import finite_loads

__all__ = ["publish", "get"]

_VERSION = 1
_MIX_TOTAL = 10_000
_SIGNAL_FIELDS = ("region", "observed", "expires", "mix", "unit_cost",
                  "carbon_intensity")
_RECORD_FIELDS = ("region", "version", "observed", "expires", "mix",
                  "unit_cost", "carbon_intensity")
_ROOT_FIELDS = ("version", "history", "idempotency", "audit")
_EVENT_FIELDS = ("key", "region", "version")
_LOCK_SUFFIX = ".lock"


class _Store:
    def __init__(self, realpath: str) -> None:
        self.realpath = realpath
        self.lock = threading.Lock()


_stores_lock = threading.Lock()
_stores: dict[str, _Store] = {}


def _get_store(path: str) -> _Store:
    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
    with _stores_lock:
        store = _stores.get(realpath)
        if store is None:
            store = _Store(realpath)
            _stores[realpath] = store
        return store


def _is_plain_int(value: object) -> bool:
    # bool is a subclass of int and must be rejected.
    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)


@contextlib.contextmanager
def _process_lock(realpath: str, *, shared: bool = False) -> Iterator[None]:
    # The companion lock file is never unlinked; the kernel releases the
    # flock on process exit, so a leftover lock never blocks a later
    # call. Equivalent real paths in different processes therefore share
    # the same exclusive lock as the per-realpath in-process lock.
    lock_path = realpath + _LOCK_SUFFIX
    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o666)
    try:
        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        try:
            yield
        finally:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def _normalize_mix(mix: object) -> dict[str, int]:
    if not isinstance(mix, dict) or not mix:
        raise ValueError("mix must be a non-empty object")
    normalized: dict[str, int] = {}
    for source, share in mix.items():
        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
            raise ValueError("mix sources must be non-empty strings")
        if not _is_plain_int(share) or share < 0:
            raise ValueError("mix shares must be non-boolean non-negative "
                             "integers")
        if source in normalized:
            raise ValueError("mix sources must be distinct")
        normalized[source] = share
    if sum(normalized.values()) != _MIX_TOTAL:
        raise ValueError("mix shares must sum to ten thousand")
    # Stored in code-point order like every other canonical mapping.
    return {source: normalized[source] for source in sorted(normalized)}


def _check_values(signal: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    region = signal["region"]
    if not isinstance(region, str) or not region:
        raise ValueError("region must be a non-empty string")

    for name in ("observed", "expires", "unit_cost", "carbon_intensity"):
        value = signal[name]
        if not _is_plain_int(value) or value < 0:
            raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a non-boolean non-negative "
                             "integer")
    if signal["expires"] < signal["observed"]:
        raise ValueError("expires must not be earlier than observed")

    signal["mix"] = _normalize_mix(signal["mix"])


def _normalize_signal(signal: object) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if not isinstance(signal, dict) \
            or set(signal.keys()) != set(_SIGNAL_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("signal must be an object with exactly region, "
                         "observed, expires, mix, unit_cost and "
                         "carbon_intensity")

    normalized: dict[str, Any] = {
        "region": signal["region"],
        "observed": signal["observed"],
        "expires": signal["expires"],
        "mix": signal["mix"],
        "unit_cost": signal["unit_cost"],
        "carbon_intensity": signal["carbon_intensity"],
    }
    _check_values(normalized)
    return normalized


def _check_sorted_keys(mapping: dict[Any, Any], label: str) -> None:
    keys = list(mapping)
    if keys != sorted(keys):
        raise ValueError(f"{label} must be ordered by key code point")


def _validate_structure(data: object) -> tuple[
    dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, str],
    dict[str, dict[str, Any]]
]:
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or set(data.keys()) != set(_ROOT_FIELDS):
        raise ValueError("signal file root must be an object with keys "
                         "version, history, idempotency and audit")

    version = data["version"]
    if not _is_plain_int(version) or version != _VERSION:
        raise ValueError("unsupported signal file version")

    history_raw = data["history"]
    idempotency_raw = data["idempotency"]
    audit_raw = data["audit"]
    if not isinstance(history_raw, dict) \
            or not isinstance(idempotency_raw, dict) \
            or not isinstance(audit_raw, dict):
        raise ValueError("history, idempotency and audit must be objects")
    _check_sorted_keys(history_raw, "history")
    _check_sorted_keys(idempotency_raw, "idempotency")
    _check_sorted_keys(audit_raw, "audit")

    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
    for region, records_raw in history_raw.items():
        if not isinstance(region, str) or not region:
            raise ValueError("regions must be non-empty strings")
        if not isinstance(records_raw, list) or not records_raw:
            raise ValueError("history must hold a non-empty record list "
                             "per region")
        records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        for index, record in enumerate(records_raw, start=1):
            if not isinstance(record, dict) \
                    or set(record.keys()) != set(_RECORD_FIELDS):
                raise ValueError("signal record has invalid fields")
            if record["region"] != region:
                raise ValueError("signal record region does not match its "
                                 "key")
            if not _is_plain_int(record["version"]) \
                    or record["version"] != index:
                raise ValueError("versions must be consecutive from 1")
            _check_values(record)
            if records and record["observed"] <= records[-1]["observed"]:
                raise ValueError("signal observations must increase across "
                                 "versions")
            records.append({
                "region": region,
                "version": index,
                "observed": record["observed"],
                "expires": record["expires"],
                "mix": dict(record["mix"]),
                "unit_cost": record["unit_cost"],
                "carbon_intensity": record["carbon_intensity"],
            })
        history[region] = records

    idempotency: dict[str, str] = {}
    for key, region in idempotency_raw.items():
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
        if not isinstance(region, str) or not region or region not in history:
            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must reference a published "
                             "region")
        idempotency[key] = region

    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    for key, event in audit_raw.items():
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
            raise ValueError("audit keys must be non-empty strings")
        if not isinstance(event, dict) \
                or set(event.keys()) != set(_EVENT_FIELDS):
            raise ValueError("signal audit event has invalid fields")
        event_key = event["key"]
        region = event["region"]
        event_version = event["version"]
        if event_key != key or not isinstance(event_key, str) or not event_key:
            raise ValueError("audit event key does not match its map key")
        if not isinstance(region, str) or not region or region not in history:
            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a published region")
        if not _is_plain_int(event_version) or event_version < 1 \
                or event_version > len(history[region]):
            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a published version")
        events[key] = {"key": event_key, "region": region,
                       "version": event_version}

    # The three sections describe one publication history: each
    # idempotency key binds one region and one publish event, the map and
    # the event agree on the region, and every published version is bound
    # to exactly one event.
    if set(idempotency) != set(events):
        raise ValueError("idempotency keys and audit events do not match")
    for key, region in idempotency.items():
        if events[key]["region"] != region:
            raise ValueError("audit event does not match its idempotency "
                             "entry")
    published = {(region, record["version"])
                 for region, records in history.items()
                 for record in records}
    bound = {(event["region"], event["version"])
             for event in events.values()}
    if bound != published:
        raise ValueError("every published version must be bound to an "
                         "audit event")

    return history, idempotency, events


def _serialize(
    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
    idempotency: dict[str, str],
    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
) -> bytes:
    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII written through, each section's
    # primary keys in code-point order, terminated by exactly one newline.
    payload = {
        "version": _VERSION,
        "history": {region: history[region] for region in sorted(history)},
        "idempotency": {key: idempotency[key] for key in sorted(idempotency)},
        "audit": {key: events[key] for key in sorted(events)},
    }
    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
    return text.encode("utf-8")


def _load_file(realpath: str) -> tuple[
    dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, str],
    dict[str, dict[str, Any]], bytes | None
]:
    try:
        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
            raw = handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return {}, {}, {}, None

    try:
        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        raise ValueError(
            f"signal file {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
    try:
        # Negative-zero and non-finite literals are format errors.
        data = finite_loads(text)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ValueError(
            f"signal file {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
    history, idempotency, events = _validate_structure(data)
    # Every read entry requires the on-disk bytes to be the canonical
    # form: fields and keys in their original order, compact JSON with
    # non-ASCII written through and exactly one trailing newline.
    if raw != _serialize(history, idempotency, events):
        raise ValueError(
            f"signal file {realpath!r} is not in canonical compact form")
    return history, idempotency, events, raw


def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
    dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
    try:
        os.fsync(dir_fd)
    finally:
        os.close(dir_fd)


def _rollback_file(realpath: str, directory: str,
                   old_bytes: bytes | None, first: BaseException) -> None:
    # Restore the exact pre-call bytes while the exclusive lock is held:
    # stage them back over the replaced file, or remove a file that did
    # not exist beforehand, then sync the directory. A failed recovery
    # surfaces chained after the original error.
    try:
        if old_bytes is None:
            try:
                os.unlink(realpath)
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass
        else:
            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
                dir=directory, prefix=".signals-restore-", suffix=".tmp")
            try:
                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
                    handle.write(old_bytes)
                    handle.flush()
                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
            except BaseException:
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
                raise
        _fsync_directory(directory)
    except OSError as recovery:
        raise recovery from first


def _commit_file(realpath: str, payload: bytes,
                 old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
    # One durable commit for the history, the idempotency map and the
    # audit event: same-directory temporary, fsync, atomic replace and a
    # directory fsync. Any failure after the replace restores the
    # pre-call bytes, so an unsuccessful publish leaves the original file
    # byte-for-byte.
    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
        dir=directory, prefix=".signals-", suffix=".tmp")
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
            handle.write(payload)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
    except BaseException:
        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
            os.unlink(tmp_path)
        raise
    try:
        _fsync_directory(directory)
    except BaseException as first:
        _rollback_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
        raise


def _publish_locked(
    realpath: str,
    normalized: dict[str, Any],
    idempotency_key: str,
    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
    idempotency: dict[str, str],
    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
    old_bytes: bytes | None,
) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], bool]:
    """Apply one publication against already loaded, locked state.

    The caller holds the per-real-path in-process lock and the
    cross-process exclusive flock and has loaded the current file with
    :func:`_load_file`; the signal has already been normalized with
    :func:`_normalize_signal`. Performs the idempotency replay check,
    appends the next version (or returns the stored record without a
    write on replay) and durably commits a first publication. Shared by
    :func:`publish` and callers that must hold several files' locks at
    once in resolved-path order.
    """
    region = normalized["region"]
    existing_region = idempotency.get(idempotency_key)
    if existing_region is not None:
        event = events[idempotency_key]
        existing = history[existing_region][event["version"] - 1]
        if {field: existing[field] for field in _SIGNAL_FIELDS} \
                != normalized:
            raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with "
                             "a different signal")
        return dict(existing), False

    versions = history.get(region)
    if versions is None:
        versions = []
        history[region] = versions
        version = 1
    else:
        if normalized["observed"] <= versions[-1]["observed"]:
            raise ValueError("signal observation must increase "
                             "across versions")
        version = versions[-1]["version"] + 1

    record: dict[str, Any] = {
        "region": region,
        "version": version,
        "observed": normalized["observed"],
        "expires": normalized["expires"],
        "mix": dict(normalized["mix"]),
        "unit_cost": normalized["unit_cost"],
        "carbon_intensity": normalized["carbon_intensity"],
    }
    versions.append(record)
    idempotency[idempotency_key] = region
    events[idempotency_key] = {
        "key": idempotency_key,
        "region": region,
        "version": version,
    }
    _commit_file(realpath,
                 _serialize(history, idempotency, events), old_bytes)
    return dict(record), True


def publish(
    path: str,
    signal: dict[str, object],
    idempotency_key: str,
) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
    """Persistently publish one live signal version.

    ``path`` and ``idempotency_key`` must be non-empty strings. The
    signal must be an object with exactly the six top-level fields
    region, observed, expires, mix, unit_cost and carbon_intensity: a
    non-empty region string, non-boolean non-negative observation and
    expiration moments (booleans rejected) with the expiration not
    earlier than the observation, non-negative unit cost and carbon
    intensity, and a non-empty energy ``mix`` object whose values are
    non-negative integers summing to exactly ten thousand. Any deviation
    raises ``ValueError`` before the file is touched.

    A first publication saves the canonical record -- the signal fields
    plus the next consecutive ``version`` for that region, starting at
    1 -- together with the idempotency binding and a publish audit event
    carrying the key, the region and the version, all three in one
    durable commit, and returns ``(record, True)``. A new version for an
    already observed region must carry a strictly later observation
    moment. Replaying the same key with an identical signal returns the
    stored record with ``False`` without adding an event or rewriting
    the file; the same key with a different signal raises
    ``ValueError`` and preserves the original bytes.

    A missing parent directory raises ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid
    existing file (encoding, JSON, negative-zero or non-finite numbers,
    version, structure, ordering, canonical bytes or references) raises
    ``ValueError``; any other locking or I/O failure raises ``OSError``.
    Calls serialize across threads and processes per resolved real path.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
    if not isinstance(idempotency_key, str) or not idempotency_key:
        raise ValueError("idempotency_key must be a non-empty string")
    normalized = _normalize_signal(signal)

    store = _get_store(path)
    with store.lock:
        # Opening the companion lock in a missing directory surfaces as
        # FileNotFoundError before the data file is created.
        with _process_lock(store.realpath):
            history, idempotency, events, old_bytes = _load_file(
                store.realpath)
            return _publish_locked(store.realpath, normalized,
                                   idempotency_key, history, idempotency,
                                   events, old_bytes)


def get(path: str, region: str, at: int) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Return the region's latest signal valid at evaluation moment ``at``.

    ``path`` and ``region`` must be non-empty strings and ``at`` a
    non-boolean non-negative integer evaluation moment, else
    ``ValueError``. The latest record whose observation is not later
    than ``at`` and whose expiration is not earlier than ``at`` is
    returned -- when several windows cover the moment, the highest
    version wins. A missing signal file raises ``FileNotFoundError``; an
    invalid file -- including non-canonical bytes -- raises
    ``ValueError``; an unknown region raises ``KeyError(region)`` and
    the absence of any valid version ``LookupError``; any other locking
    or I/O failure raises ``OSError``. The call never writes, and the
    returned record is a fresh copy with region, version, observed,
    expires, mix, unit_cost and carbon_intensity.
    """
    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
    if not isinstance(region, str) or not region:
        raise ValueError("region must be a non-empty string")
    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
        raise ValueError("at must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")

    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
    with _process_lock(realpath, shared=True):
        history, _idempotency, _events, raw = _load_file(realpath)
    if raw is None:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"signal file {realpath!r} does not exist")
    versions = history.get(region)
    if versions is None:
        raise KeyError(region)

    valid: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    for record in versions:
        if record["observed"] <= at <= record["expires"]:
            valid = record
    if valid is None:
        raise LookupError(region)
    result = dict(valid)
    result["mix"] = dict(valid["mix"])
    return result

2	
3	One on-disk document (version 1) holds the whole supply side of the
4	market:
5	
6	* ``history`` maps each resource id to its published records, versions
7	  consecutive from 1 and starts strictly increasing across versions;
8	* ``idempotency`` binds each publish key to the resource it carried;
9	* ``audit`` holds one publish event per first publication, binding the
10	  idempotency key, the resource id and the version it created.

185	
186	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] = {}
187	    for resource_id, records_raw in history_raw.items():
188	        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
189	            raise ValueError("resource ids must be non-empty strings")
190	        if not isinstance(records_raw, list) or not records_raw:
191	            raise ValueError("history must hold a non-empty record list "
192	                             "per resource")
193	        records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
194	        for index, record in enumerate(records_raw, start=1):
195	            if not isinstance(record, dict) \
196	                    or set(record.keys()) != set(_RECORD_FIELDS):
197	                raise ValueError("resource record has invalid fields")
198	            if record["resource_id"] != resource_id:
199	                raise ValueError("resource record id does not match its key")
200	            if not _is_plain_int(record["version"]) \
201	                    or record["version"] != index:
202	                raise ValueError("versions must be consecutive from 1")
203	            _check_values(record)
204	            if records and record["start"] <= records[-1]["start"]:
205	                raise ValueError("resource starts must increase across "
206	                                 "versions")
207	            records.append({
208	                "resource_id": resource_id,
209	                "version": index,
210	                "region": record["region"],
211	                "capacity": record["capacity"],
212	                "start": record["start"],
213	                "end": record["end"],
214	                "unit_cost": record["unit_cost"],
215	                "carbon_intensity": record["carbon_intensity"],
216	                "residency": list(record["residency"]),
217	            })
218	        history[resource_id] = records
219	
220	    idempotency: dict[str, str] = {}
221	    for key, resource_id in idempotency_raw.items():
222	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
223	            raise ValueError("idempotency keys must be non-empty strings")
224	        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id \
225	                or resource_id not in history:
226	            raise ValueError("idempotency entry must reference a published "
227	                             "resource")
228	        idempotency[key] = resource_id
229	
230	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
231	    for key, event in audit_raw.items():
232	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
233	            raise ValueError("audit keys must be non-empty strings")
234	        if not isinstance(event, dict) \
235	                or set(event.keys()) != set(_EVENT_FIELDS):
236	            raise ValueError("publish audit event has invalid fields")
237	        event_key = event["key"]
238	        resource_id = event["resource_id"]
239	        event_version = event["version"]
240	        if event_key != key or not isinstance(event_key, str) or not event_key:
241	            raise ValueError("audit event key does not match its map key")
242	        if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id \
243	                or resource_id not in history:
244	            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a published "
245	                             "resource")
246	        if not _is_plain_int(event_version) or event_version < 1 \
247	                or event_version > len(history[resource_id]):
248	            raise ValueError("audit event must reference a published "
249	                             "version")
250	        events[key] = {"key": event_key, "resource_id": resource_id,
251	                       "version": event_version}
252	
253	    # The three sections describe one publication history: each
254	    # idempotency key binds one resource and one publish event, the map
255	    # and the event agree on the resource, and every published version
256	    # is bound to exactly one event.
257	    if set(idempotency) != set(events):
258	        raise ValueError("idempotency keys and audit events do not match")
259	    for key, resource_id in idempotency.items():
260	        if events[key]["resource_id"] != resource_id:
261	            raise ValueError("audit event does not match its idempotency "
262	                             "entry")
263	    published = {(resource_id, record["version"])
264	                 for resource_id, records in history.items()
265	                 for record in records}
266	    bound = {(event["resource_id"], event["version"])
267	             for event in events.values()}
268	    if bound != published:
269	        raise ValueError("every published version must be bound to an "
270	                         "audit event")
271	
272	    return history, idempotency, events

275	def _canonical_bytes(
276	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
277	    idempotency: dict[str, str],
278	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
279	) -> bytes:
280	    # The canonical wire form every reader accepts: compact UTF-8 JSON
281	    # with non-ASCII written through, sections in their fixed field order
282	    # and each section's primary keys in code-point order, terminated by
283	    # exactly one newline. The round trip also rejects duplicate keys
284	    # (json.loads keeps the last occurrence) and any escaping of
285	    # non-ASCII characters that json.dumps would write through.
286	    return _serialize(history, idempotency, events)

289	def _load_file(realpath: str) -> tuple[
290	    dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]], dict[str, str],
291	    dict[str, dict[str, Any]], bytes | None
292	]:
293	    try:
294	        with open(realpath, "rb") as handle:
295	            raw = handle.read()
296	    except FileNotFoundError:
297	        return {}, {}, {}, None
298	
299	    try:
300	        text = raw.decode("utf-8")
301	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
302	        raise ValueError(
303	            f"supply file {realpath!r} is not valid UTF-8") from exc
304	    try:
305	        # Negative-zero and non-finite literals are format errors.
306	        data = finite_loads(text)
307	    except ValueError as exc:
308	        raise ValueError(
309	            f"supply file {realpath!r} is not valid JSON") from exc
310	    history, idempotency, events = _validate_structure(data)
311	    # Every read entry requires the on-disk bytes to be the canonical
312	    # form: fields and keys in their original order, compact JSON with
313	    # non-ASCII written through and exactly one trailing newline. Any
314	    # extra whitespace, escaped non-ASCII character, reordered field or
315	    # missing/duplicated final newline is a ValueError.
316	    if raw != _canonical_bytes(history, idempotency, events):
317	        raise ValueError(
318	            f"supply file {realpath!r} is not in canonical compact form")
319	    return history, idempotency, events, raw

322	def _serialize(
323	    history: dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]],
324	    idempotency: dict[str, str],
325	    events: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
326	) -> bytes:
327	    # Compact UTF-8 JSON, non-ASCII written through, each section's
328	    # primary keys in code-point order, terminated by exactly one newline.
329	    payload = {
330	        "version": _VERSION,
331	        "history": {resource_id: history[resource_id]
332	                    for resource_id in sorted(history)},
333	        "idempotency": {key: idempotency[key] for key in sorted(idempotency)},
334	        "audit": {key: events[key] for key in sorted(events)},
335	    }
336	    text = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"),
337	                      allow_nan=False) + "\n"
338	    return text.encode("utf-8")

349	def _rollback_file(realpath: str, directory: str,
350	                   old_bytes: bytes | None, first: BaseException) -> None:
351	    # Restore the exact pre-call bytes while the exclusive lock is held:
352	    # stage them back over the replaced file, or remove a file that did
353	    # not exist beforehand, then sync the directory. A failed recovery
354	    # surfaces chained after the original error.
355	    try:
356	        if old_bytes is None:
357	            try:
358	                os.unlink(realpath)
359	            except FileNotFoundError:
360	                pass
361	        else:
362	            fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
363	                dir=directory, prefix=".resources-restore-", suffix=".tmp")
364	            try:
365	                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
366	                    handle.write(old_bytes)
367	                    handle.flush()
368	                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
369	                os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
370	            except BaseException:
371	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
372	                    os.unlink(tmp_path)
373	                raise
374	        _fsync_directory(directory)
375	    except OSError as recovery:
376	        raise recovery from first

379	def _commit_file(realpath: str, payload: bytes,
380	                 old_bytes: bytes | None) -> None:
381	    # One durable commit for the history, the idempotency map and the
382	    # audit event: same-directory temporary, fsync, atomic replace and a
383	    # directory fsync. Any failure after the replace restores the
384	    # pre-call bytes, so an unsuccessful publish leaves the original file
385	    # byte-for-byte.
386	    directory = os.path.dirname(realpath) or "."
387	    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
388	        dir=directory, prefix=".resources-", suffix=".tmp")
389	    try:
390	        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
391	            handle.write(payload)
392	            handle.flush()
393	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
394	        os.replace(tmp_path, realpath)
395	    except BaseException:
396	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
397	            os.unlink(tmp_path)
398	        raise
399	    try:
400	        _fsync_directory(directory)
401	    except BaseException as first:
402	        _rollback_file(realpath, directory, old_bytes, first)
403	        raise

406	def publish(
407	    path: str,
408	    resource: dict[str, object],
409	    idempotency_key: str,
410	) -> tuple[dict[str, object], bool]:
411	    """Persistently publish one resource-supply version.
412	
413	    ``path`` and ``idempotency_key`` must be non-empty strings. The
414	    resource must be an object with exactly the eight top-level fields
415	    resource_id, region, capacity, start, end, unit_cost,
416	    carbon_intensity and residency: non-empty id and region strings, a
417	    positive integer capacity, non-negative start, end, unit_cost and
418	    carbon_intensity (booleans rejected) with start not later than end,
419	    and a non-empty residency list of distinct non-empty strings sorted
420	    by code point that contains the resource's own region. Any
421	    deviation raises ``ValueError`` before the file is touched.
422	
423	    A first publication saves the canonical record -- the resource
424	    fields plus the next consecutive ``version`` for that resource id,
425	    starting at 1 -- together with the idempotency binding and a
426	    publish audit event carrying the key, the resource id and the
427	    version, all three in one durable commit, and returns
428	    ``(record, True)``. A new version of an already published resource
429	    must carry a strictly later start than the current latest version.
430	    Replaying the same key with an identical resource returns the
431	    stored record with ``False`` without adding an event or rewriting
432	    the file; the same key with a different resource raises
433	    ``ValueError`` and preserves the original bytes.
434	
435	    A missing parent directory raises ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid
436	    existing file (encoding, JSON, negative-zero or non-finite numbers,
437	    version, structure, ordering, canonical bytes or references) raises
438	    ``ValueError``; any other locking or I/O failure raises ``OSError``.
439	    Calls serialize across threads and processes per resolved real path.
440	    """
441	    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
442	        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
443	    if not isinstance(idempotency_key, str) or not idempotency_key:
444	        raise ValueError("idempotency_key must be a non-empty string")
445	    normalized = _normalize_resource(resource)
446	    resource_id = normalized["resource_id"]
447	
448	    store = _get_store(path)
449	    with store.lock:
450	        # Opening the companion lock in a missing directory surfaces as
451	        # FileNotFoundError before the data file is created.
452	        with _process_lock(store.realpath):
453	            history, idempotency, events, old_bytes = _load_file(
454	                store.realpath)
455	
456	            existing_id = idempotency.get(idempotency_key)
457	            if existing_id is not None:
458	                event = events[idempotency_key]
459	                existing = history[existing_id][event["version"] - 1]
460	                if {field: existing[field]
461	                        for field in _RESOURCE_FIELDS} != normalized:
462	                    raise ValueError("idempotency key was already used with "
463	                                     "a different resource")
464	                return dict(existing), False
465	
466	            versions = history.get(resource_id)
467	            if versions is None:
468	                versions = []
469	                history[resource_id] = versions
470	                version = 1
471	            else:
472	                if normalized["start"] <= versions[-1]["start"]:
473	                    raise ValueError("resource start must increase across "
474	                                     "versions")
475	                version = versions[-1]["version"] + 1
476	
477	            record: dict[str, Any] = {
478	                "resource_id": resource_id,
479	                "version": version,
480	                "region": normalized["region"],
481	                "capacity": normalized["capacity"],
482	                "start": normalized["start"],
483	                "end": normalized["end"],
484	                "unit_cost": normalized["unit_cost"],
485	                "carbon_intensity": normalized["carbon_intensity"],
486	                "residency": list(normalized["residency"]),
487	            }
488	            versions.append(record)
489	            idempotency[idempotency_key] = resource_id
490	            events[idempotency_key] = {
491	                "key": idempotency_key,
492	                "resource_id": resource_id,
493	                "version": version,
494	            }
495	            _commit_file(store.realpath,
496	                         _serialize(history, idempotency, events), old_bytes)
497	            return dict(record), True
498

500	def get(
501	    path: str,
502	    resource_id: str,
503	    version: int | None = None,
504	) -> dict[str, object]:
505	    """Return a read-only copy of one published resource record.
506	
507	    ``path`` and ``resource_id`` must be non-empty strings and
508	    ``version``, when given, a non-boolean positive integer, else
509	    ``ValueError``. Without ``version`` the latest record of the
510	    resource is returned. A missing supply file raises
511	    ``FileNotFoundError``; an invalid file -- including non-canonical
512	    bytes -- raises ``ValueError``; an unknown resource id raises
513	    ``KeyError(resource_id)`` and an unknown version
514	    ``KeyError(version)``; any other locking or I/O failure raises
515	    ``OSError``. The call never writes, and the returned record is a
516	    fresh copy with resource_id, version, region, capacity, start, end,
517	    unit_cost, carbon_intensity and residency.
518	    """
519	    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
520	        raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
521	    if not isinstance(resource_id, str) or not resource_id:
522	        raise ValueError("resource_id must be a non-empty string")
523	    if version is not None \
524	            and (not _is_plain_int(version) or version <= 0):
525	        raise ValueError("version must be a non-boolean positive integer")
526	
527	    realpath = os.path.realpath(path)
528	    with _process_lock(realpath, shared=True):
529	        history, _idempotency, _events, raw = _load_file(realpath)
530	    if raw is None:
531	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"supply file {realpath!r} does not exist")
532	    versions = history.get(resource_id)
533	    if versions is None:
534	        raise KeyError(resource_id)
535	    if version is None:
536	        return dict(versions[-1])
537	    if version > len(versions):
538	        raise KeyError(version)
539	    return dict(versions[version - 1])

541	def feasible(
542	    job_path: str,
543	    supply_path: str,
544	    job_id: str,
545	    at: int,
546	) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
547	    """Rank the resources that can serve one accepted job at ``at``.
548	
549	    ``job_path`` and ``supply_path`` must be non-empty strings,
550	    ``job_id`` a non-empty string and ``at`` a non-boolean non-negative
551	    integer evaluation moment, else ``ValueError``. The job file must be
552	    a ``jobs.submit`` acceptance file -- a version-1 ``jobs.register``
553	    file is invalid structure -- and both files are read as complete
554	    snapshots while their shared locks are held together.
555	
556	    A missing acceptance or supply file raises ``FileNotFoundError``;
557	    an invalid file -- including a supply file outside canonical
558	    compact form -- raises ``ValueError``; an unknown job id raises
559	    ``KeyError(job_id)``; any other locking or I/O failure raises
560	    ``OSError``.
561	
562	    Each resource contributes only its highest version valid at ``at``
563	    (start not later than ``at`` not later than end). A candidate must
564	    sit in one of the job's regions, offer at least the job's work as
565	    capacity, cover the job's residency regions with its own residency
566	    list, and stay available at least until the job's deadline. The
567	    total cost is the job's work times the unit cost and the total
568	    carbon the work times the carbon intensity; a candidate exceeding
569	    the job's max_cost or carbon_cap budget is excluded. The result is
570	    ordered by carbon intensity, then unit cost, then resource id, each
571	    entry carrying the resource record and both totals; with no
572	    candidate the list is empty.
573	    """
574	    if not isinstance(job_path, str) or not job_path:
575	        raise ValueError("job_path must be a non-empty string")
576	    if not isinstance(supply_path, str) or not supply_path:
577	        raise ValueError("supply_path must be a non-empty string")
578	    if not isinstance(job_id, str) or not job_id:
579	        raise ValueError("job_id must be a non-empty string")
580	    if not _is_plain_int(at) or at < 0:
581	        raise ValueError("at must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")
582	
583	    job_real = os.path.realpath(job_path)
584	    supply_real = os.path.realpath(supply_path)
585	    # Lock both snapshots together, in a path order shared by every
586	    # caller, so concurrent calls can never deadlock.
587	    with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
588	        for locked in sorted({job_real, supply_real}):
589	            stack.enter_context(_process_lock(locked, shared=True))
590	
591	        accepted, _job_map, _job_events, job_raw = _jobs._load_submit_file(
592	            job_real)
593	        if job_raw is None:
594	            raise FileNotFoundError(
595	                f"acceptance file {job_real!r} does not exist")
596	        history, _idempotency, _events, supply_raw = _load_file(supply_real)
597	        if supply_raw is None:
598	            raise FileNotFoundError(
599	                f"supply file {supply_real!r} does not exist")
600	
601	        job = accepted.get(job_id)
602	        if job is None:
603	            raise KeyError(job_id)
604	
605	        work = job["work"]
606	        regions = set(job["regions"])
607	        residency = set(job["residency"])
608	        candidates: list[dict[str, object]] = []
609	        for records in history.values():
610	            active: dict[str, Any] | None = None
611	            for record in records:
612	                if record["start"] <= at <= record["end"]:
613	                    active = record
614	            if active is None:
615	                continue
616	            if active["region"] not in regions:
617	                continue
618	            if active["capacity"] < work:
619	                continue
620	            if not residency <= set(active["residency"]):
621	                continue
622	            if active["end"] < job["deadline"]:
623	                continue
624	            total_cost = work * active["unit_cost"]
625	            total_carbon = work * active["carbon_intensity"]
626	            if total_cost > job["max_cost"] \
627	                    or total_carbon > job["carbon_cap"]:
628	                continue
629	            candidates.append({
630	                "resource": dict(active),
631	                "total_cost": total_cost,
632	                "total_carbon": total_carbon,
633	            })
634	
635	    candidates.sort(key=lambda entry: (entry["resource"]["carbon_intensity"],
636	                                       entry["resource"]["unit_cost"],
637	                                       entry["resource"]["resource_id"]))
638	    return candidates
